references.text: Pharaoh asks Moses to pray to the Lord to remove the plagues, a recurring pattern where Pharaoh seeks intercession during the plagues.
Pharaoh again asks Moses to pray for him and promises to let the people go, but hardens his heart afterward.
Pharaoh admits his sin and asks Moses and Aaron to pray to the Lord to stop the plague, using similar wording about 'bearing sin'.
The context where Pharaoh calls on Moses and Aaron and confesses his sin against the Lord and against them.
Use of the expression 'שָׂא נָא' (forgive now) in connection with bearing or forgiving sin.
Moses is asked to forgive the people's sin using similar wording, 'שָׂא נָא', for forgiveness.
Saul asks Samuel to forgive his sin using the same expression 'שָׂא נָא אֶת־חַטָּאתִי'.
Job is asked to pray for his friends, interceding on behalf of others as a parallel to Moses' role.
Both verses link the acknowledgment of sin directly to a prayer for forgiveness from God.
Both verses link the admission of personal sin directly to a prayer for healing or grace.
